summary:
I checked all five files I own for leftover Linux/POSIX code and compiled each one under the strict MSYS2 GCC 16 recipe. Nothing needed changing, and all five compile with zero errors and zero warnings.

Starting state: `git diff HEAD --stat` showed no earlier agent had edited these files, and `git diff main HEAD` showed none since the branch point either.

What the search covered: unistd/fcntl/sys includes, g_spawn/GSubprocess, g_unix_*, gdk_x11/GDK_BACKEND, file://, getenv/HOME, '/' path assumptions, stat/fopen/open, pthread/fork/popen, long/off_t sizes, strerror/errno, CSS font-family strings, and Linux wording (PulseAudio/PipeWire/pactl/Wayland/X11/run-radios/flatpak). None of these appear in the five files. The only '/' strings are SDBASE HTTP endpoint paths (/v1/workflows/...), not file paths.
- **Time zones:** the two call sites (local_event_prepare.c:370 and player_rotation.c:257) already use `radios_time_zone_new()` and already include `radios/platform.h`.
- **No CSS:** none of these files contains CSS strings or font-family lists, so the D5 font rule has nothing to change here.
- **Other checks:**
  - local_event_prepare.c builds its dates from gint64 microsecond timestamps and runs its HTTP calls on a GTask worker thread.
  - player_rotation.c and player_scope_execution.c copy into fixed-size char buffers only with g_strlcpy/g_snprintf, and their deck arrays have 32 slots, matching the 32-player limit in player_topology.h (RADIOS_PLAYER_TOPOLOGY_MAX_PLAYERS).
  - The `long double` at neon_progress.c:174 is only used for a multiplication, and on MinGW x64 it is the same 80-bit type as on Linux x86_64, as build-system.md notes.
  - The ATK accessibility calls in neon_progress.c and library_analysis_ui.c are harmless no-ops on Windows, since GTK 3 has no Windows accessibility bridge.
  - All Turkish UI texts are unchanged.
api: No public API changes. The files keep their existing contracts: radios_library_analysis_ui_page_new; radios_local_event_prepare_async and radios_local_event_prepare_schema_async; radios_neon_progress_new / _set_state / _get_state / _set_seek_callback plus the "seek-begin" signal; radios_player_rotation_open, radios_player_weekly_open and the related functions; the RadioSPlayerScopeExecution API.
verification: Compiled each of the five files once with the strict standalone recipe from ENV_CLOUD.md: x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc (MSYS2 GCC 16 under Wine) -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 -D_WIN32_WINNT=0x0A00 -DWINVER=0x0A00 -DUNICODE -D_UNICODE -I/home/user/RadioSs/include plus ucrt64-pkg-config cflags (glib/gio/gio-windows/gtk3/json-glib/curl/ffmpeg), -c only. Output: /opt/radios-port/work/c-ui-sweep-p8/{library_analysis_ui,local_event_prepare,neon_progress,player_rotation,player_scope_execution}.o. All five exited 0 with no diagnostics.
Grep sweep of the five files for POSIX/Linux constructs, Linux UI wording, CSS font-family strings and time-zone calls: nothing left to convert.
As instructed, nothing was linked or run and no tests were executed.
open_issues: Two time-zone fallbacks behave differently and were left as they were. local_event_prepare.c:369-371 silently falls back to UTC when the calendar's 'timezone' is empty or unknown. player_rotation.c:256-258 instead fails with 'Şemanın saat dilimi geçersiz.' when radios_time_zone_new() returns NULL, which includes a present-but-empty 'timezone' member. On Windows, radios_time_zone_new() rejects non-IANA ids (Windows registry names, POSIX strings), so a calendar saved with such an id would hit these paths. Calendars are expected to carry IANA ids validated by the service.

Not verified here: neon_progress drag/keyboard seeking (including AltGr behaviour under GDK-Win32) and the GUI tests native_library_analysis, native_neon_progress, the local_event_prepare UI tests and autoplay_execution_clock. These need to run on the user's Windows PC.
